items.q: The values 16, 18, 43, 67, 68 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: Arranged in order the third value is the median, so the median is 43.

items.q: The values 67, 30, 30, 30, 62, 66 were recorded. State the mode.
items.s: The value 30 occurs three times, more often than any other, so the mode is 30.

items.q: The values 3, 59, 64, 88, 89 were recorded. Calculate the range.
items.s: Range = largest - smallest = 89 - 3 = 86.

items.q: A box contains 5 red and 5 black balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.s: The box holds 10 balls in all, so P(red) = 5/10 = 0.5.

items.q: The probability that an event happens is 0.35. Calculate the probability that it does not happen.
The values 5, 20, 38, 41, 60, 75 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: With six values the median is the mean of the third and fourth: (38 + 41)/2 = 39.5.

items.q: A grouped frequency table has midpoint 35 with frequency 9; midpoint 45 with frequency 3; midpoint 95 with frequency 8. Calculate the mean of the distribution.
items.s: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 1210 and total frequency = 20, so the mean is 1210/20 = 60.5.

items.q: A class of 14 students has a mean score of 55 while another class of 17 students has a mean score of 77. Calculate the mean score of the two classes combined.
The values 5, 8, 10, 29, 35 form a complete population. Calculate the population variance.
items.s: The mean is 17.4. Sum of squared deviations is 741.2, so the variance is that sum divided by 5 = 148.2.

items.q: The values 9, 16, 18, 27, 31, 32 are a sample drawn from a large population. Calculate the sample variance.
items.s: The mean is 22.17 and the sum of squared deviations is 426.8. Dividing by n - 1 = 5 gives 85.37.

items.q: The values 14, 19, 20, 27, 29 are a sample. Calculate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 21.8, the sum of squared deviations is 150.8, and the variance is 37.7. Its square root gives a standard deviation of 6.14.

items.q: A distribution has a mean of 81 and a standard deviation of 10. Calculate its coefficient of variation in percent.
items.s: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (10/81) x 100 = 12.35 percent.

items.q: The values 30, 38, 51, 64, 67, 68, 70 are arranged in order. Taking the second and sixth values as the lower and upper quartiles, calculate the quartile deviation.
items.s: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2 = (68 - 38)/2 = 15.

items.q: A bag holds 20 balls of which 6 are red and 7 are blue. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red or blue?
items.s: Red and blue are mutually exclusive, so P = 6/20 + 7/20 = 0.65.

items.q: In a class, the probability that a student offers Physics is 5/10 and the probability that a student offers Chemistry is 6/10. The probability of offering both is 1/10. What is the probability that a student offers Physics or Chemistry?
Two events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.7. Calculate P(A and B).
items.s: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 0.3 x 0.7 = 0.21.

items.q: In how many ways can 5 distinct objects be arranged taken 2 at a time?
items.s: The number of arrangements is 5P2 = 5!/(5 - 2)! = 20.

items.q: In how many ways can a committee of 2 be chosen from 6 people?
items.s: The number of committees is 6C2 = 6!/(2!(6 - 2)!) = 15.

items.q: From 12 students a team of 2 is to be selected for a quiz and then 4 of the remaining students for a debate. In how many ways can both selections be made?
items.s: Choose the quiz team in 12C2 = 66 ways, then the debaters in 10C4 = 210 ways, so the total is 66 x 210 = 13860.

items.q: A fair experiment is repeated 5 times and the probability of success in a single trial is 0.3. Calculate the probability of exactly 2 successes.
A binomial variable has 18 trials with probability of success 0.5 in each trial. Calculate its mean.
items.s: Mean = np = 18 x 0.5 = 9.

items.q: A binomial variable has 16 trials with probability of success 0.25 in each trial. Calculate its variance.
items.s: Variance = np(1 - p) = 16 x 0.25 x 0.75 = 3.

items.q: The number of calls arriving at a switchboard follows a Poisson distribution with mean 3 per minute. Calculate the probability of exactly 0 calls in a minute.
A Poisson variable has a mean of 1.5 occurrences per unit time. State its variance.
items.s: For a Poisson distribution the variance equals the mean, so the variance is 1.5.

items.q: A normally distributed variable has mean 100 and standard deviation 10. Calculate the standard score of the value 120.
items.s: z = (x - mean)/standard deviation = (120 - 100)/10 = 2.

items.q: A normal variable has mean 50 and standard deviation 4. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413 and between the mean and two standard deviations is 0.4772, find the probability that a value is less than 54.
items.s: The value 54 is 1 standard deviation(s) above the mean, so the probability is 0.5 + 0.3413 = 0.8413.

items.q: A normal variable has mean 50 and standard deviation 5. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413, find the probability that a value lies between 45 and 55.
items.s: Both limits are one standard deviation from the mean, so the probability is 2 x 0.3413 = 0.6826.

items.q: For 6 pairs of observations the sums of squares and products about the means are: sum of xy about the means = 49, sum of x squared about the mean = 47 and sum of y squared about the mean = 81. Calculate the coefficient of correlation.
items.s: r = sum(xy)/sqrt(sum(x squared) x sum(y squared)) = 49/sqrt(47 x 81) = 0.7942.

items.q: For a set of paired observations the sum of xy about the means is 79 and the sum of x squared about the mean is 57. Calculate the slope of the regression line of y on x.
items.s: Slope b = sum(xy)/sum(x squared) = 79/57 = 1.39.

items.q: The regression line of y on x is y = 9 + 1.5x. Estimate the value of y when x = 5.
items.s: Substituting x = 5 gives y = 9 + 1.5 x 5 = 16.5.

items.q: A sample of 4 observations is drawn from a population with standard deviation 8. Calculate the standard error of the sample mean.
items.s: Standard error = standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 8/sqrt(4) = 4.

items.q: A sample of 25 has a known population standard deviation of 12. Taking the standard normal value as 1.96 for the required confidence level, calculate the half width of the confidence interval for the mean.
items.s: Half width = z x standard deviation/sqrt(n) = 1.96 x 12/sqrt(25) = 4.7.

items.q: A survey must estimate a mean to within 3 units with standard normal value 2, the population standard deviation being 12. Calculate the smallest sample size needed.
items.s: n = (z x standard deviation / margin)^2 = (2 x 12/3)^2 = 64, so the sample must be at least 64.

items.q: A discrete variable takes the values 0, 1 and 2 with probabilities 0.25, 0.5 and 0.25 respectively. Calculate its standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 1 and the variance is 0.5, so the standard deviation is 0.7071.

items.q: The scores obtained by five students in a test are 15, 20, 26, 33, 35. Calculate the mean score.
items.s: Mean = sum of scores / number of scores = 129 / 5 = 25.8.

items.q: The values 25, 44, 59, 64, 69 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: Arranged in order the third value is the median, so the median is 59.

items.q: The values 44, 45, 8, 8, 31, 8 were recorded. State the mode.
items.s: The value 8 occurs three times, more often than any other, so the mode is 8.

items.q: The values 47, 70, 73, 75, 89 were recorded. Calculate the range.
items.s: Range = largest - smallest = 89 - 47 = 42.

items.q: A box contains 7 red and 9 black balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.s: The box holds 16 balls in all, so P(red) = 7/16 = 0.4375.

items.q: The probability that an event happens is 0.45. Calculate the probability that it does not happen.
The values 14, 15, 23, 35, 57, 79 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: With six values the median is the mean of the third and fourth: (23 + 35)/2 = 29.

items.q: A grouped frequency table has midpoint 5 with frequency 3; midpoint 65 with frequency 6; midpoint 95 with frequency 7. Calculate the mean of the distribution.
items.s: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 1070 and total frequency = 16, so the mean is 1070/16 = 66.88.

items.q: A class of 9 students has a mean score of 53 while another class of 8 students has a mean score of 85. Calculate the mean score of the two classes combined.
The values 3, 5, 8, 17, 21 form a complete population. Calculate the population variance.
items.s: The mean is 10.8. Sum of squared deviations is 244.8, so the variance is that sum divided by 5 = 48.96.

items.q: The values 4, 15, 22, 27, 31, 39 are a sample drawn from a large population. Calculate the sample variance.
items.s: The mean is 23 and the sum of squared deviations is 762. Dividing by n - 1 = 5 gives 152.4.

items.q: The values 18, 20, 25, 26, 34 are a sample. Calculate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 24.6, the sum of squared deviations is 155.2, and the variance is 38.8. Its square root gives a standard deviation of 6.23.

items.q: A distribution has a mean of 41 and a standard deviation of 6. Calculate its coefficient of variation in percent.
items.s: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (6/41) x 100 = 14.63 percent.

items.q: The values 7, 30, 43, 45, 48, 58, 74 are arranged in order. Taking the second and sixth values as the lower and upper quartiles, calculate the quartile deviation.
items.s: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2 = (58 - 30)/2 = 14.

items.q: A bag holds 20 balls of which 4 are red and 3 are blue. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red or blue?
items.s: Red and blue are mutually exclusive, so P = 4/20 + 3/20 = 0.35.

items.q: In a class, the probability that a student offers Physics is 5/10 and the probability that a student offers Chemistry is 5/10. The probability of offering both is 1/10. What is the probability that a student offers Physics or Chemistry?
Two events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.5 and P(B) = 0.5. Calculate P(A and B).
items.s: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 0.5 x 0.5 = 0.25.

items.q: In how many ways can 8 distinct objects be arranged taken 4 at a time?
items.s: The number of arrangements is 8P4 = 8!/(8 - 4)! = 1680.

items.q: In how many ways can a committee of 2 be chosen from 10 people?
items.s: The number of committees is 10C2 = 10!/(2!(10 - 2)!) = 45.

items.q: From 9 students a team of 2 is to be selected for a quiz and then 4 of the remaining students for a debate. In how many ways can both selections be made?
items.s: Choose the quiz team in 9C2 = 36 ways, then the debaters in 7C4 = 35 ways, so the total is 36 x 35 = 1260.

items.q: A fair experiment is repeated 6 times and the probability of success in a single trial is 0.3. Calculate the probability of exactly 1 successes.
A binomial variable has 10 trials with probability of success 0.5 in each trial. Calculate its mean.
items.s: Mean = np = 10 x 0.5 = 5.

items.q: A binomial variable has 13 trials with probability of success 0.3 in each trial. Calculate its variance.
The number of calls arriving at a switchboard follows a Poisson distribution with mean 2 per minute. Calculate the probability of exactly 1 calls in a minute.
A Poisson variable has a mean of 3 occurrences per unit time. State its variance.
items.s: For a Poisson distribution the variance equals the mean, so the variance is 3.

items.q: A normally distributed variable has mean 70 and standard deviation 10. Calculate the standard score of the value 60.
items.s: z = (x - mean)/standard deviation = (60 - 70)/10 = -1.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines relative frequency probability?
o: the difference between the upper and the lower quartile of an ordered set of data
the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions
a number between minus one and plus one that measures the strength and direction of a straight line relationship
a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
items.s: relative frequency probability: the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions. The other options describe relative dispersion, product moment coefficient, interquartile range.

items.q: cumulative probability may be defined as
o: the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all
a strong link between two quantities that arises only because both are driven by a third quantity
items.s: cumulative probability: the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value. The other options describe spurious association, equally likely outcomes, impossible event.

items.q: Which term is described by “a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises”?
o: negative association
extrapolation
positive association
product moment coefficient
items.s: positive association is a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises.

items.q: Which of the following best describes unbiased estimator?
o: a measure of dispersion that keeps the original units of the data
the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question
a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value
the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
items.s: unbiased estimator: a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value. The other options describe absolute measure of spread, complementary event, mean squared deviation.

items.q: least squares may be defined as
o: the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it
the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible
a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
items.s: least squares: the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible. The other options describe extrapolation, open end class, midpoint.

items.q: The statement “the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large” describes which of the following?
o: standard normal variable
normal table
normal approximation
standardisation
items.s: normal approximation is the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines population.
o: a method in which every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen and every group of the required size has an equal chance
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises
the single average obtained for two or more groups after pooling their totals and their counts
items.s: population: the whole set of items about which information is wanted. The other options describe negative association, simple random selection, combined average.

items.q: normal curve may be defined as
o: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises
a continuous bell shaped curve that is symmetric about its centre and fixed by its mean and its spread
items.s: normal curve: a continuous bell shaped curve that is symmetric about its centre and fixed by its mean and its spread. The other options describe cluster selection, negative association, mean squared deviation.

items.q: The statement “an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once” describes which of the following?
o: circular arrangement
counting principle
factorial
arrangement with repetition
items.s: circular arrangement is an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once.

items.q: Which term is described by “an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population”?
o: non sampling error
parameter
stratified selection
statistic
items.s: non sampling error is an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population.

items.q: Which term is described by “the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used”?
o: sampling distribution
sampling error
sample
cluster selection
items.s: sampling error is the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used.

items.q: Which term is described by “a method in which a starting point is chosen at random and every kth member of the list is then taken”?
o: systematic selection
sampling distribution
population
sampling error
items.s: systematic selection is a method in which a starting point is chosen at random and every kth member of the list is then taken.

items.q: Which term is described by “the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them”?
o: degrees of freedom
mean squared deviation
relative dispersion
sample variance
items.s: mean squared deviation is the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them.

items.q: Which term is described by “the point on the bell curve where it changes from bending downwards to bending upwards, found one standard deviation from the centre”?
o: normal approximation
inflection point
tail area
standard score
items.s: inflection point is the point on the bell curve where it changes from bending downwards to bending upwards, found one standard deviation from the centre.

items.q: Poisson approximation may be defined as
o: a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance
one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts
the use of a count distribution with mean equal to the product of trials and chance when the number of trials is large and the chance of success is small
a continuous bell shaped curve that is symmetric about its centre and fixed by its mean and its spread
items.s: Poisson approximation: the use of a count distribution with mean equal to the product of trials and chance when the number of trials is large and the chance of success is small. The other options describe decile, normal curve, discrete random variable.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines normal approximation?
o: an observation that lies far away from the rest of the data and pulls an average towards it
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
items.s: normal approximation: the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large. The other options describe Poisson process, Bernoulli trial, outlier.

items.q: The statement “two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening” describes which of the following?
o: subjective probability
independent events
conditional probability
impossible event
items.s: independent events is two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening.

items.q: Which term is described by “the single average obtained for two or more groups after pooling their totals and their counts”?
o: open end class
positively skewed distribution
combined average
median
items.s: combined average is the single average obtained for two or more groups after pooling their totals and their counts.

items.q: The statement “one of the three values that divide an ordered set of data into four equal parts” describes which of the following?
o: percentile
mode
quartile
median
items.s: quartile is one of the three values that divide an ordered set of data into four equal parts.

items.q: grouped average may be defined as
o: a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance
the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average
items.s: grouped average: the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies. The other options describe discrete random variable, random experiment, parameter.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines conditional probability.
o: one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
items.s: conditional probability: the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened. The other options describe random experiment, geometric average, percentile.

items.q: The statement “outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment” describes which of the following?
o: sample space
equally likely outcomes
multiplication rule
random experiment
items.s: equally likely outcomes is outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment.

items.q: arrangement with repetition may be defined as
o: a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate
an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order
a measure of dispersion that keeps the original units of the data
a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
items.s: arrangement with repetition: an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order. The other options describe confidence interval, exhaustive events, absolute measure of spread.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines subjective probability?
o: the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways
a degree of belief assigned to an event by a judge rather than derived from counting or repetition
the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment
the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data
items.s: subjective probability: a degree of belief assigned to an event by a judge rather than derived from counting or repetition. The other options describe mode, counting principle, sample space.

items.q: Which term is described by “a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode”?
o: arithmetic mean
outlier
positively skewed distribution
percentile
items.s: positively skewed distribution is a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode.

items.q: The statement “the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets” describes which of the following?
o: coefficient of variation
mean squared deviation
quartile deviation
population variance
items.s: coefficient of variation is the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines negative association.
o: an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all
a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once
items.s: negative association: a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises. The other options describe population, circular arrangement, impossible event.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines decile.
o: the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both
one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
items.s: decile: one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts. The other options describe range, classical probability, addition rule.

items.q: positive association may be defined as
o: a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value
items.s: positive association: a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises. The other options describe open end class, conditional probability, point estimate.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways”?
o: binomial coefficient
factorial
combination
counting principle
items.s: counting principle is the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways.

items.q: Which term is described by “a method in which interviewers fill fixed numbers of respondents in stated categories, without random drawing”?
o: point estimate
quota selection
cluster selection
population
items.s: quota selection is a method in which interviewers fill fixed numbers of respondents in stated categories, without random drawing.

items.q: Which term is described by “a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide”?
o: quartile
symmetrical distribution
negatively skewed distribution
decile
items.s: symmetrical distribution is a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines relative dispersion.
o: a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
the use of a count distribution with mean equal to the product of trials and chance when the number of trials is large and the chance of success is small
items.s: relative dispersion: a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared. The other options describe Bernoulli trial, Poisson approximation, cluster selection.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines stratified selection?
o: a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises
a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size
the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible
the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment
items.s: stratified selection: a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size. The other options describe negative association, sample space, least squares.

items.q: binomial setting may be defined as
o: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all
items.s: binomial setting: a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes. The other options describe normal approximation, mean squared deviation, impossible event.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines standard normal variable.
o: a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one
a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide
an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once
the slope of the line that estimates one quantity from the other
items.s: standard normal variable: a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one. The other options describe circular arrangement, symmetrical distribution, regression coefficient.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines regression line?
o: the whole set of items about which information is wanted
the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other
a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value
a part of a population selected so that conclusions can be drawn about the whole
items.s: regression line: the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other. The other options describe sample, statistic, population.

items.q: Which term is described by “a number between minus one and plus one that measures the strength and direction of a straight line relationship”?
o: scatter diagram
positive association
product moment coefficient
extrapolation
items.s: product moment coefficient is a number between minus one and plus one that measures the strength and direction of a straight line relationship.

items.q: The statement “a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode” describes which of the following?
o: weighted mean
negatively skewed distribution
open end class
positively skewed distribution
items.s: positively skewed distribution is a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines tail area?
o: the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
items.s: tail area: the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value. The other options describe margin of error, weighted mean, cluster selection.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines zero association.
o: the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
a relationship in which no tendency for the two quantities to move together can be seen
a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
items.s: zero association: a relationship in which no tendency for the two quantities to move together can be seen. The other options describe positive association, open end class, standardisation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines symmetrical distribution.
o: a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide
the square of the correlation coefficient, giving the proportion of the variation in one quantity explained by the other
a continuous bell shaped curve that is symmetric about its centre and fixed by its mean and its spread
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
items.s: symmetrical distribution: a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide. The other options describe midpoint, normal curve, coefficient of determination.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines extrapolation?
o: a degree of belief assigned to an event by a judge rather than derived from counting or repetition
a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value
the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
items.s: extrapolation: the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it. The other options describe unbiased estimator, midpoint, subjective probability.

items.q: degrees of freedom may be defined as
o: a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
the number of standard deviations by which a value lies above or below the mean
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
items.s: degrees of freedom: the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data. The other options describe standard score, normal approximation, normal table.

items.q: empirical rule may be defined as
o: the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three
the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
items.s: empirical rule: the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three. The other options describe sample variance, random experiment, classical probability.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines absolute measure of spread.
o: the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order
a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate
a measure of dispersion that keeps the original units of the data
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
items.s: absolute measure of spread: a measure of dispersion that keeps the original units of the data. The other options describe binomial coefficient, normal table, confidence interval.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines decile?
o: a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide
a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts
items.s: decile: one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts. The other options describe midpoint, symmetrical distribution, positive association.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines equally likely outcomes.
o: half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile
the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
items.s: equally likely outcomes: outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment. The other options describe normal table, margin of error, quartile deviation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines coefficient of variation.
o: the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions
a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
items.s: coefficient of variation: the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets. The other options describe discrete random variable, relative frequency probability, equally likely outcomes.

items.q: Which term is described by “outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment”?
o: addition rule
equally likely outcomes
sample space
relative frequency probability
items.s: equally likely outcomes is outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment.

items.q: Which of the following best describes relative dispersion?
o: the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
items.s: relative dispersion: a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared. The other options describe regression line, classical probability, midpoint.

items.q: confidence interval may be defined as
o: the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data
a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
items.s: confidence interval: a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate. The other options describe population, random experiment, mode.

items.q: event may be defined as
o: the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both
the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
items.s: event: a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest. The other options describe midpoint, binomial coefficient, addition rule.

items.q: The statement “an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population” describes which of the following?
o: systematic selection
quota selection
non sampling error
sample
items.s: non sampling error is an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines random experiment?
o: the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
items.s: random experiment: a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out. The other options describe tail area, standardisation, standard error.

items.q: Which term is described by “one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts”?
o: mode
quartile
decile
geometric average
items.s: decile is one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines open end class?
o: a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
items.s: open end class: a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption. The other options describe standardisation, event, degrees of freedom.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines multiplication rule?
o: the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
the relation that the chance of two events happening together is the chance of the first times the conditional chance of the second
a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate
items.s: multiplication rule: the relation that the chance of two events happening together is the chance of the first times the conditional chance of the second. The other options describe normal approximation, confidence interval, addition rule.

items.q: geometric average may be defined as
o: a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value
the total of all the observations divided by the number of observations
the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change
items.s: geometric average: the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change. The other options describe arithmetic mean, event, unbiased estimator.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines point estimate.
o: a degree of belief assigned to an event by a judge rather than derived from counting or repetition
a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value
a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
items.s: point estimate: a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value. The other options describe standardisation, binomial setting, subjective probability.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines cluster selection?
o: a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other
items.s: cluster selection: a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used. The other options describe parameter, Poisson process, regression line.

items.q: sample variance may be defined as
o: one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts
the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations
the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible
the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both
items.s: sample variance: the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations. The other options describe least squares, decile, addition rule.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines midpoint?
o: a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide
the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
a method in which interviewers fill fixed numbers of respondents in stated categories, without random drawing
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
items.s: midpoint: the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval. The other options describe grouped average, symmetrical distribution, quota selection.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines empirical rule?
o: a table, formula or graph that gives the chance of each value of a random variable
the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used
a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value
the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three
items.s: empirical rule: the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three. The other options describe probability distribution, unbiased estimator, sampling error.

items.q: The statement “the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes” describes which of the following?
o: sample space
subjective probability
independent events
classical probability
items.s: classical probability is the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes.

items.q: A grouped frequency table has midpoint 35 with frequency 4; midpoint 65 with frequency 8; midpoint 85 with frequency 4. Calculate the mean of the distribution.
items.s: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 1000 and total frequency = 16, so the mean is 1000/16 = 62.5.

items.q: The values 4, 7, 13, 28, 35 form a complete population. Calculate the population variance.
items.s: The mean is 17.4. Sum of squared deviations is 729.2, so the variance is that sum divided by 5 = 145.8.

items.q: A distribution has a mean of 48 and a standard deviation of 4. Calculate its coefficient of variation in percent.
items.s: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (4/48) x 100 = 8.33 percent.

items.q: A bag holds 20 balls of which 6 are red and 2 are blue. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red or blue?
items.s: Red and blue are mutually exclusive, so P = 6/20 + 2/20 = 0.4.

items.q: Two events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.2. Calculate P(A and B).
items.s: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 0.3 x 0.2 = 0.06.

items.q: In how many ways can 7 distinct objects be arranged taken 4 at a time?
items.s: The number of arrangements is 7P4 = 7!/(7 - 4)! = 840.

items.q: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 11 people?
items.s: The number of committees is 11C3 = 11!/(3!(11 - 3)!) = 165.

items.q: A binomial variable has 16 trials with probability of success 0.3 in each trial. Calculate its mean.
A binomial variable has 11 trials with probability of success 0.2 in each trial. Calculate its variance.
A Poisson variable has a mean of 4 occurrences per unit time. State its variance.
items.s: For a Poisson distribution the variance equals the mean, so the variance is 4.

items.q: A normally distributed variable has mean 60 and standard deviation 12. Calculate the standard score of the value 84.
items.s: z = (x - mean)/standard deviation = (84 - 60)/12 = 2.

items.q: The regression line of y on x is y = 2 + 2x. Estimate the value of y when x = 5.
items.s: Substituting x = 5 gives y = 2 + 2 x 5 = 12.

items.q: A sample of 9 observations is drawn from a population with standard deviation 15. Calculate the standard error of the sample mean.
items.s: Standard error = standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 15/sqrt(9) = 5.

items.q: The scores obtained by five students in a test are 10, 24, 35, 57, 59. Calculate the mean score.
items.s: Mean = sum of scores / number of scores = 185 / 5 = 37.

items.q: The values 18, 41, 47, 63, 66 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: Arranged in order the third value is the median, so the median is 47.

items.q: The values 53, 16, 16, 60, 68, 16 were recorded. State the mode.
items.s: The value 16 occurs three times, more often than any other, so the mode is 16.

items.q: A class of 10 students has a mean score of 53 while another class of 13 students has a mean score of 77. Calculate the mean score of the two classes combined.
The values 24, 27, 42, 53, 61 were recorded. Calculate the range.
items.s: Range = largest - smallest = 61 - 24 = 37.

items.q: The values 11, 15, 24, 26, 28, 30 are a sample drawn from a large population. Calculate the sample variance.
items.s: The mean is 22.33 and the sum of squared deviations is 289.3. Dividing by n - 1 = 5 gives 57.87.

items.q: The values 9, 19, 22, 23, 30 are a sample. Calculate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 20.6, the sum of squared deviations is 233.2, and the variance is 58.3. Its square root gives a standard deviation of 7.64.

items.q: The values 20, 23, 34, 39, 42, 47, 76 are arranged in order. Taking the second and sixth values as the lower and upper quartiles, calculate the quartile deviation.
items.s: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2 = (47 - 23)/2 = 12.

items.q: A box contains 6 red and 3 black balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.s: The box holds 9 balls in all, so P(red) = 6/9 = 0.6667.

items.q: In a class, the probability that a student offers Physics is 5/10 and the probability that a student offers Chemistry is 3/10. The probability of offering both is 2/10. What is the probability that a student offers Physics or Chemistry?
From 8 students a team of 3 is to be selected for a quiz and then 5 of the remaining students for a debate. In how many ways can both selections be made?
items.s: Choose the quiz team in 8C3 = 56 ways, then the debaters in 5C5 = 1 ways, so the total is 56 x 1 = 56.

items.q: The number of calls arriving at a switchboard follows a Poisson distribution with mean 1 per minute. Calculate the probability of exactly 2 calls in a minute.

A normal variable has mean 40 and standard deviation 5. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413 and between the mean and two standard deviations is 0.4772, find the probability that a value is less than 50.
items.s: The value 50 is 2 standard deviation(s) above the mean, so the probability is 0.5 + 0.4772 = 0.9772.

items.q: A normal variable has mean 70 and standard deviation 5. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413, find the probability that a value lies between 65 and 75.
items.s: Both limits are one standard deviation from the mean, so the probability is 2 x 0.3413 = 0.6826.

items.q: For 5 pairs of observations the sums of squares and products about the means are: sum of xy about the means = 52, sum of x squared about the mean = 69 and sum of y squared about the mean = 63. Calculate the coefficient of correlation.
items.s: r = sum(xy)/sqrt(sum(x squared) x sum(y squared)) = 52/sqrt(69 x 63) = 0.7887.

items.q: For a set of paired observations the sum of xy about the means is 70 and the sum of x squared about the mean is 56. Calculate the slope of the regression line of y on x.
items.s: Slope b = sum(xy)/sum(x squared) = 70/56 = 1.25.

items.q: A sample of 25 has a known population standard deviation of 10. Taking the standard normal value as 2.58 for the required confidence level, calculate the half width of the confidence interval for the mean.
items.s: Half width = z x standard deviation/sqrt(n) = 2.58 x 10/sqrt(25) = 5.16.

items.q: A survey must estimate a mean to within 5 units with standard normal value 2, the population standard deviation being 12. Calculate the smallest sample size needed.
items.s: n = (z x standard deviation / margin)^2 = (2 x 12/5)^2 = 23.04, so the sample must be at least 24.

items.q: The values 4, 6, 19, 34, 43, 64 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: With six values the median is the mean of the third and fourth: (19 + 34)/2 = 26.5.

items.q: A grouped frequency table has midpoint 35 with frequency 6; midpoint 55 with frequency 8; midpoint 95 with frequency 6. Calculate the mean of the distribution.
items.s: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 1220 and total frequency = 20, so the mean is 1220/20 = 61.

items.q: The values 6, 21, 28, 34, 36 form a complete population. Calculate the population variance.
items.s: The mean is 25. Sum of squared deviations is 588, so the variance is that sum divided by 5 = 117.6.

items.q: A distribution has a mean of 72 and a standard deviation of 10. Calculate its coefficient of variation in percent.
items.s: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (10/72) x 100 = 13.89 percent.

items.q: A bag holds 20 balls of which 7 are red and 7 are blue. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red or blue?
items.s: Red and blue are mutually exclusive, so P = 7/20 + 7/20 = 0.7.

items.q: Two events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.5 and P(B) = 0.7. Calculate P(A and B).
items.s: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 0.5 x 0.7 = 0.35.

items.q: In how many ways can 9 distinct objects be arranged taken 2 at a time?
items.s: The number of arrangements is 9P2 = 9!/(9 - 2)! = 72.

items.q: In how many ways can a committee of 5 be chosen from 7 people?
items.s: The number of committees is 7C5 = 7!/(5!(7 - 5)!) = 21.

items.q: A binomial variable has 20 trials with probability of success 0.3 in each trial. Calculate its mean.
items.s: Mean = np = 20 x 0.3 = 6.

items.q: A binomial variable has 13 trials with probability of success 0.4 in each trial. Calculate its variance.
A normally distributed variable has mean 50 and standard deviation 12. Calculate the standard score of the value 38.
items.s: z = (x - mean)/standard deviation = (38 - 50)/12 = -1.

items.q: The regression line of y on x is y = 7 + 1.5x. Estimate the value of y when x = 11.
items.s: Substituting x = 11 gives y = 7 + 1.5 x 11 = 23.5.

items.q: A sample of 9 observations is drawn from a population with standard deviation 8. Calculate the standard error of the sample mean.
items.s: Standard error = standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 8/sqrt(9) = 2.67.

items.q: The scores obtained by five students in a test are 5, 18, 23, 36, 38. Calculate the mean score.
items.s: Mean = sum of scores / number of scores = 120 / 5 = 24.

items.q: The values 21, 22, 44, 55, 62 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: Arranged in order the third value is the median, so the median is 44.

items.q: The values 6, 37, 6, 53, 6, 68 were recorded. State the mode.
items.s: The value 6 occurs three times, more often than any other, so the mode is 6.

items.q: A class of 18 students has a mean score of 46 while another class of 14 students has a mean score of 66. Calculate the mean score of the two classes combined.
The values 22, 29, 49, 56, 70 were recorded. Calculate the range.
items.s: Range = largest - smallest = 70 - 22 = 48.

items.q: The values 7, 15, 21, 30, 32, 39 are a sample drawn from a large population. Calculate the sample variance.
items.s: The mean is 24 and the sum of squared deviations is 704. Dividing by n - 1 = 5 gives 140.8.

items.q: The values 9, 12, 13, 24, 41 are a sample. Calculate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 19.8, the sum of squared deviations is 690.8, and the variance is 172.7. Its square root gives a standard deviation of 13.14.

items.q: The values 8, 23, 29, 39, 41, 59, 75 are arranged in order. Taking the second and sixth values as the lower and upper quartiles, calculate the quartile deviation.
items.s: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2 = (59 - 23)/2 = 18.

items.q: A box contains 6 red and 7 black balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.s: The box holds 13 balls in all, so P(red) = 6/13 = 0.4615.

items.q: In a class, the probability that a student offers Physics is 6/10 and the probability that a student offers Chemistry is 4/10. The probability of offering both is 1/10. What is the probability that a student offers Physics or Chemistry?
From 13 students a team of 3 is to be selected for a quiz and then 5 of the remaining students for a debate. In how many ways can both selections be made?
items.s: Choose the quiz team in 13C3 = 286 ways, then the debaters in 10C5 = 252 ways, so the total is 286 x 252 = 72072.

items.q: A fair experiment is repeated 5 times and the probability of success in a single trial is 0.2. Calculate the probability of exactly 2 successes.

A normal variable has mean 60 and standard deviation 4. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413 and between the mean and two standard deviations is 0.4772, find the probability that a value is less than 68.
items.s: The value 68 is 2 standard deviation(s) above the mean, so the probability is 0.5 + 0.4772 = 0.9772.

items.q: For 5 pairs of observations the sums of squares and products about the means are: sum of xy about the means = 47, sum of x squared about the mean = 65 and sum of y squared about the mean = 55. Calculate the coefficient of correlation.
items.s: r = sum(xy)/sqrt(sum(x squared) x sum(y squared)) = 47/sqrt(65 x 55) = 0.7861.

items.q: For a set of paired observations the sum of xy about the means is 62 and the sum of x squared about the mean is 22. Calculate the slope of the regression line of y on x.
items.s: Slope b = sum(xy)/sum(x squared) = 62/22 = 2.82.

items.q: A sample of 49 has a known population standard deviation of 15. Taking the standard normal value as 1.96 for the required confidence level, calculate the half width of the confidence interval for the mean.
items.s: Half width = z x standard deviation/sqrt(n) = 1.96 x 15/sqrt(49) = 4.2.

items.q: Which term is described by “a selection of objects in which the order of the objects does not matter”?
o: circular arrangement
combination
permutation
factorial
items.s: combination is a selection of objects in which the order of the objects does not matter.

items.q: In this course, grouped average refers to
o: the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
the single average obtained for two or more groups after pooling their totals and their counts
the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data
items.s: grouped average: the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies. The other options describe mode, combined average, median.

items.q: Which term is described by “an observation that lies far away from the rest of the data and pulls an average towards it”?
o: geometric average
mode
decile
outlier
items.s: outlier is an observation that lies far away from the rest of the data and pulls an average towards it.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure”
o: Bernoulli trial
binomial setting
cumulative probability
discrete random variable
items.s: Bernoulli trial is a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure.

items.q: regression line is best described as
o: a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises
the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other
a strong link between two quantities that arises only because both are driven by a third quantity
a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
items.s: regression line: the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other. The other options describe negative association, positive association, spurious association.

items.q: Which term is described by “the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size”?
o: sampling error
sampling frame
standard error
non sampling error
items.s: standard error is the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size.

items.q: parameter is best described as
o: a complete list of the members of a population from which a selection is made
an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population
a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average
the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used
items.s: parameter: a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average. The other options describe sampling frame, sampling error, non sampling error.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what unbiased estimator means.
o: an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population
the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size
a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value
a part of a population selected so that conclusions can be drawn about the whole
items.s: unbiased estimator: a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value. The other options describe standard error, non sampling error, sample.

items.q: In this course, relative frequency probability refers to
o: a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all
the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions
the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both
items.s: relative frequency probability: the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions. The other options describe addition rule, impossible event, event.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a relationship in which no tendency for the two quantities to move together can be seen”
o: rank correlation
zero association
least squares
spurious association
items.s: zero association is a relationship in which no tendency for the two quantities to move together can be seen.

items.q: positive association is best described as
o: the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it
a relationship in which no tendency for the two quantities to move together can be seen
a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible
items.s: positive association: a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises. The other options describe extrapolation, zero association, least squares.

items.q: The best definition of sample among these is
o: a method in which a starting point is chosen at random and every kth member of the list is then taken
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
a part of a population selected so that conclusions can be drawn about the whole
the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size
items.s: sample: a part of a population selected so that conclusions can be drawn about the whole. The other options describe cluster selection, standard error, systematic selection.

items.q: The best definition of empirical rule among these is
o: the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three
the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean
items.s: empirical rule: the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three. The other options describe standard deviation, population variance, range.

items.q: Which term is described by “a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate”?
o: systematic selection
unbiased estimator
statistic
confidence interval
items.s: confidence interval is a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what arrangement with repetition means.
o: the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order
an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order
an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters
the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number
items.s: arrangement with repetition: an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order. The other options describe permutation, factorial, binomial coefficient.

items.q: decile is best described as
o: the number of observations divided by the sum of their reciprocals, used for average speeds
the single average obtained for two or more groups after pooling their totals and their counts
the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts
items.s: decile: one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts. The other options describe harmonic average, combined average, grouped average.

items.q: Which term is described by “the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it”?
o: regression coefficient
extrapolation
scatter diagram
negative association
items.s: extrapolation is the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it.

items.q: All of the following belong to Measures of dispersion EXCEPT
o: normal curve
range
interquartile range
quartile deviation
items.s: Every other option belongs to Measures of dispersion. “normal curve” belongs to The normal distribution, not Measures of dispersion.

items.q: The statement “a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate” describes which of the following?
o: Poisson process
Bernoulli trial
expected value
cumulative probability
items.s: Poisson process is a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the number of observations divided by the sum of their reciprocals, used for average speeds”
o: combined average
decile
harmonic average
symmetrical distribution
items.s: harmonic average is the number of observations divided by the sum of their reciprocals, used for average speeds.

items.q: The statement “the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size” describes which of the following?
o: standard error
stratified selection
unbiased estimator
margin of error
items.s: standard error is the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what exhaustive events means.
o: the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all
two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening
items.s: exhaustive events: a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment. The other options describe impossible event, conditional probability, independent events.

items.q: In this course, binomial coefficient refers to
o: an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters
the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number
the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways
the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order
items.s: binomial coefficient: the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order. The other options describe factorial, counting principle, permutation.

items.q: mean squared deviation is best described as
o: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three
the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
items.s: mean squared deviation: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them. The other options describe population variance, range, empirical rule.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the pattern of values a statistic would take if the same sized samples were drawn again and again”
o: unbiased estimator
margin of error
sampling distribution
sampling frame
items.s: sampling distribution is the pattern of values a statistic would take if the same sized samples were drawn again and again.

items.q: In this course, event refers to
o: two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening
a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment
a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
items.s: event: a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest. The other options describe exhaustive events, independent events, sample space.

items.q: In this course, population variance refers to
o: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets
the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
items.s: population variance: the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean. The other options describe coefficient of variation, range, mean squared deviation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the slope of the line that estimates one quantity from the other”?
o: zero association
regression coefficient
spurious association
extrapolation
items.s: regression coefficient is the slope of the line that estimates one quantity from the other.

items.q: Which term is described by “an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all”?
o: relative frequency probability
equally likely outcomes
impossible event
exhaustive events
items.s: impossible event is an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an observation that lies far away from the rest of the data and pulls an average towards it”
o: combined average
outlier
open end class
midpoint
items.s: outlier is an observation that lies far away from the rest of the data and pulls an average towards it.

items.q: The best definition of Poisson process among these is
o: a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance
the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
items.s: Poisson process: a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate. The other options describe Bernoulli trial, discrete random variable, cumulative probability.

items.q: In this course, sampling error refers to
o: the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population
a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value
the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used
items.s: sampling error: the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used. The other options describe point estimate, non sampling error, margin of error.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data”
o: relative dispersion
degrees of freedom
range
absolute measure of spread
items.s: degrees of freedom is the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets”
o: coefficient of variation
population variance
standard deviation
degrees of freedom
items.s: coefficient of variation is the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets.

items.q: The statement “a complete list of the members of a population from which a selection is made” describes which of the following?
o: confidence interval
population
sampling frame
sampling distribution
items.s: sampling frame is a complete list of the members of a population from which a selection is made.

items.q: The statement “the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions” describes which of the following?
o: relative frequency probability
complementary event
subjective probability
addition rule
items.s: relative frequency probability is the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions.

items.q: The best definition of central limit result among these is
o: the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
the statement that the average of a large number of independent observations is approximately normally distributed whatever the shape of the original data
the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
items.s: central limit result: the statement that the average of a large number of independent observations is approximately normally distributed whatever the shape of the original data. The other options describe normal approximation, tail area, standardisation.

items.q: The best definition of standard score among these is
o: the number of standard deviations by which a value lies above or below the mean
the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one
items.s: standard score: the number of standard deviations by which a value lies above or below the mean. The other options describe tail area, normal table, standard normal variable.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value”
o: sample
non sampling error
statistic
point estimate
items.s: statistic is a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value.

items.q: The statement “a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value” describes which of the following?
o: population
systematic selection
sampling error
point estimate
items.s: point estimate is a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value.

items.q: The statement “a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises” describes which of the following?
o: negative association
extrapolation
scatter diagram
least squares
items.s: negative association is a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises.

items.q: In this course, mean deviation refers to
o: the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean
the average of the absolute differences between each observation and a chosen average
a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
items.s: mean deviation: the average of the absolute differences between each observation and a chosen average. The other options describe standard deviation, degrees of freedom, relative dispersion.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other”
o: spurious association
scatter diagram
regression line
positive association
items.s: regression line is the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other.

items.q: standard deviation is best described as
o: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
a measure of dispersion that keeps the original units of the data
the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean
