items.s: standard deviation: the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean. The other options describe absolute measure of spread, mean squared deviation, relative dispersion.

items.q: In this course, cluster selection refers to
o: the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
a method in which every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen and every group of the required size has an equal chance
an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
items.s: cluster selection: a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used. The other options describe non sampling error, margin of error, simple random selection.

items.q: The best definition of statistic among these is
o: a complete list of the members of a population from which a selection is made
a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value
a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
items.s: statistic: a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value. The other options describe point estimate, sampling frame, cluster selection.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what quartile means.
o: the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
one of the three values that divide an ordered set of data into four equal parts
items.s: quartile: one of the three values that divide an ordered set of data into four equal parts. The other options describe percentile, weighted mean, mode.

items.q: Which term is described by “a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size”?
o: margin of error
quota selection
stratified selection
population
items.s: stratified selection is a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size.

items.q: In this course, interquartile range refers to
o: the difference between the upper and the lower quartile of an ordered set of data
the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets
a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
items.s: interquartile range: the difference between the upper and the lower quartile of an ordered set of data. The other options describe coefficient of variation, standard deviation, relative dispersion.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used”
o: systematic selection
cluster selection
non sampling error
margin of error
items.s: cluster selection is a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used.

items.q: The best definition of percentile among these is
o: the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data
one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
items.s: percentile: one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts. The other options describe grouped average, weighted mean, mode.

items.q: circular arrangement is best described as
o: an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order
an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once
the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways
the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order
items.s: circular arrangement: an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once. The other options describe arrangement with repetition, counting principle, binomial coefficient.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what population means.
o: a method in which a starting point is chosen at random and every kth member of the list is then taken
an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
items.s: population: the whole set of items about which information is wanted. The other options describe non sampling error, margin of error, systematic selection.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption”
o: open end class
combined average
negatively skewed distribution
weighted mean
items.s: open end class is a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption.

items.q: population is best described as
o: the whole set of items about which information is wanted
the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size
the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used
the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
items.s: population: the whole set of items about which information is wanted. The other options describe sampling error, standard error, margin of error.

items.q: The best definition of inflection point among these is
o: the point on the bell curve where it changes from bending downwards to bending upwards, found one standard deviation from the centre
the statement that the average of a large number of independent observations is approximately normally distributed whatever the shape of the original data
the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one
items.s: inflection point: the point on the bell curve where it changes from bending downwards to bending upwards, found one standard deviation from the centre. The other options describe standard normal variable, standardisation, central limit result.

items.q: symmetrical distribution is best described as
o: the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change
a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide
items.s: symmetrical distribution: a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide. The other options describe midpoint, geometric average, open end class.

items.q: All of the following belong to Sampling and estimation EXCEPT
o: coefficient of variation
parameter
sample
population
items.s: Every other option belongs to Sampling and estimation. “coefficient of variation” belongs to Measures of dispersion, not Sampling and estimation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order”?
o: permutation
arrangement with repetition
binomial coefficient
factorial
items.s: binomial coefficient is the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order.

items.q: Which term is described by “the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other”?
o: negative association
regression line
product moment coefficient
coefficient of determination
items.s: regression line is the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other.

items.q: grouped average is best described as
o: the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
items.s: grouped average: the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies. The other options describe open end class, weighted mean, median.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what normal table means.
o: the statement that the average of a large number of independent observations is approximately normally distributed whatever the shape of the original data
the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
items.s: normal table: a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration. The other options describe standard normal variable, central limit result, tail area.

items.q: mode is best described as
o: the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data
one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
one of the three values that divide an ordered set of data into four equal parts
the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
items.s: mode: the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data. The other options describe quartile, median, percentile.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what regression line means.
o: the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible
the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other
the slope of the line that estimates one quantity from the other
a plot of paired observations that shows whether the two quantities move together
items.s: regression line: the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other. The other options describe least squares, regression coefficient, scatter diagram.

items.q: The statement “the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value” describes which of the following?
o: expected value
binomial setting
Poisson approximation
discrete random variable
items.s: expected value is the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value.

items.q: The values 17, 22, 27, 31, 34, 37 are a sample drawn from a large population. Calculate the sample variance.
items.s: The mean is 28 and the sum of squared deviations is 284. Dividing by n - 1 = 5 gives 56.8.

items.q: The values 13, 17, 30, 33, 40 are a sample. Calculate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 26.6, the sum of squared deviations is 509.2, and the variance is 127.3. Its square root gives a standard deviation of 11.28.

items.q: The values 7, 32, 53, 54, 66, 68, 72 are arranged in order. Taking the second and sixth values as the lower and upper quartiles, calculate the quartile deviation.
items.s: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2 = (68 - 32)/2 = 18.

items.q: In a class, the probability that a student offers Physics is 4/10 and the probability that a student offers Chemistry is 5/10. The probability of offering both is 1/10. What is the probability that a student offers Physics or Chemistry?
A fair experiment is repeated 3 times and the probability of success in a single trial is 0.25. Calculate the probability of exactly 1 successes.

A normal variable has mean 40 and standard deviation 10. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413 and between the mean and two standard deviations is 0.4772, find the probability that a value is less than 50.
items.s: The value 50 is 1 standard deviation(s) above the mean, so the probability is 0.5 + 0.3413 = 0.8413.

items.q: For a set of paired observations the sum of xy about the means is 91 and the sum of x squared about the mean is 32. Calculate the slope of the regression line of y on x.
items.s: Slope b = sum(xy)/sum(x squared) = 91/32 = 2.84.

items.q: The scores obtained by five students in a test are 6, 14, 17, 20, 49. Calculate the mean score.
items.s: Mean = sum of scores / number of scores = 106 / 5 = 21.2.

items.q: The values 7, 27, 48, 62, 68 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: Arranged in order the third value is the median, so the median is 48.

items.q: The values 2, 10, 13, 23, 28, 37 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: With six values the median is the mean of the third and fourth: (13 + 23)/2 = 18.

items.q: The values 20, 20, 35, 65, 47, 20 were recorded. State the mode.
items.s: The value 20 occurs three times, more often than any other, so the mode is 20.

items.q: A grouped frequency table has midpoint 35 with frequency 2; midpoint 45 with frequency 2; midpoint 85 with frequency 8. Calculate the mean of the distribution.
items.s: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 840 and total frequency = 12, so the mean is 840/12 = 70.

items.q: The values 23, 24, 58, 81, 88 were recorded. Calculate the range.
items.s: Range = largest - smallest = 88 - 23 = 65.

items.q: The values 12, 19, 23, 27, 34 form a complete population. Calculate the population variance.
items.s: The mean is 23. Sum of squared deviations is 274, so the variance is that sum divided by 5 = 54.8.

items.q: A distribution has a mean of 62 and a standard deviation of 4. Calculate its coefficient of variation in percent.
items.s: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (4/62) x 100 = 6.45 percent.

items.q: A box contains 9 red and 9 black balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.s: The box holds 18 balls in all, so P(red) = 9/18 = 0.5.

items.q: A bag holds 20 balls of which 7 are red and 4 are blue. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red or blue?
items.s: Red and blue are mutually exclusive, so P = 7/20 + 4/20 = 0.55.

items.q: Two events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.2. Calculate P(A and B).
items.s: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 0.4 x 0.2 = 0.08.

items.q: The probability that an event happens is 0.4. Calculate the probability that it does not happen.
In how many ways can 5 distinct objects be arranged taken 4 at a time?
items.s: The number of arrangements is 5P4 = 5!/(5 - 4)! = 120.

items.q: In how many ways can a committee of 2 be chosen from 7 people?
items.s: The number of committees is 7C2 = 7!/(2!(7 - 2)!) = 21.

items.q: From 12 students a team of 2 is to be selected for a quiz and then 5 of the remaining students for a debate. In how many ways can both selections be made?
items.s: Choose the quiz team in 12C2 = 66 ways, then the debaters in 10C5 = 252 ways, so the total is 66 x 252 = 16632.

items.q: A binomial variable has 19 trials with probability of success 0.25 in each trial. Calculate its mean.
A binomial variable has 11 trials with probability of success 0.4 in each trial. Calculate its variance.
The number of calls arriving at a switchboard follows a Poisson distribution with mean 1 per minute. Calculate the probability of exactly 0 calls in a minute.
A normally distributed variable has mean 100 and standard deviation 12. Calculate the standard score of the value 124.
items.s: z = (x - mean)/standard deviation = (124 - 100)/12 = 2.

items.q: For 6 pairs of observations the sums of squares and products about the means are: sum of xy about the means = 41, sum of x squared about the mean = 47 and sum of y squared about the mean = 56. Calculate the coefficient of correlation.
items.s: r = sum(xy)/sqrt(sum(x squared) x sum(y squared)) = 41/sqrt(47 x 56) = 0.7992.

items.q: The regression line of y on x is y = 3 + 3x. Estimate the value of y when x = 8.
items.s: Substituting x = 8 gives y = 3 + 3 x 8 = 27.

items.q: A sample of 25 observations is drawn from a population with standard deviation 9. Calculate the standard error of the sample mean.
items.s: Standard error = standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 9/sqrt(25) = 1.8.

items.q: A sample of 36 has a known population standard deviation of 12. Taking the standard normal value as 1.96 for the required confidence level, calculate the half width of the confidence interval for the mean.
items.s: Half width = z x standard deviation/sqrt(n) = 1.96 x 12/sqrt(36) = 3.92.

items.q: A survey must estimate a mean to within 5 units with standard normal value 1.96, the population standard deviation being 15. Calculate the smallest sample size needed.
items.s: n = (z x standard deviation / margin)^2 = (1.96 x 15/5)^2 = 34.57, so the sample must be at least 35.

items.q: A class of 11 students has a mean score of 44 while another class of 14 students has a mean score of 80. Calculate the mean score of the two classes combined.
The values 15, 18, 21, 26, 36, 37 are a sample drawn from a large population. Calculate the sample variance.
items.s: The mean is 25.5 and the sum of squared deviations is 429.5. Dividing by n - 1 = 5 gives 85.9.

items.q: The values 4, 13, 21, 34, 41 are a sample. Calculate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 22.6, the sum of squared deviations is 909.2, and the variance is 227.3. Its square root gives a standard deviation of 15.08.

items.q: The values 12, 21, 44, 53, 60, 61, 68 are arranged in order. Taking the second and sixth values as the lower and upper quartiles, calculate the quartile deviation.
items.s: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2 = (61 - 21)/2 = 20.

items.q: A fair experiment is repeated 5 times and the probability of success in a single trial is 0.25. Calculate the probability of exactly 1 successes.

A normal variable has mean 50 and standard deviation 10. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413 and between the mean and two standard deviations is 0.4772, find the probability that a value is less than 70.
items.s: The value 70 is 2 standard deviation(s) above the mean, so the probability is 0.5 + 0.4772 = 0.9772.

items.q: A normal variable has mean 60 and standard deviation 5. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413, find the probability that a value lies between 55 and 65.
items.s: Both limits are one standard deviation from the mean, so the probability is 2 x 0.3413 = 0.6826.

items.q: For a set of paired observations the sum of xy about the means is 82 and the sum of x squared about the mean is 51. Calculate the slope of the regression line of y on x.
items.s: Slope b = sum(xy)/sum(x squared) = 82/51 = 1.61.

items.q: The scores obtained by five students in a test are 5, 9, 10, 27, 38. Calculate the mean score.
items.s: Mean = sum of scores / number of scores = 89 / 5 = 17.8.

items.q: The values 15, 18, 47, 61, 69 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: Arranged in order the third value is the median, so the median is 47.

items.q: The values 2, 10, 14, 21, 41, 45 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: With six values the median is the mean of the third and fourth: (14 + 21)/2 = 17.5.

items.q: The values 66, 43, 8, 8, 8, 37 were recorded. State the mode.
items.s: The value 8 occurs three times, more often than any other, so the mode is 8.

items.q: A grouped frequency table has midpoint 35 with frequency 8; midpoint 75 with frequency 4; midpoint 85 with frequency 3. Calculate the mean of the distribution.
items.s: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 835 and total frequency = 15, so the mean is 835/15 = 55.67.

items.q: The values 9, 10, 56, 58, 65 were recorded. Calculate the range.
items.s: Range = largest - smallest = 65 - 9 = 56.

items.q: The values 5, 8, 13, 28, 29 form a complete population. Calculate the population variance.
items.s: The mean is 16.6. Sum of squared deviations is 505.2, so the variance is that sum divided by 5 = 101.

items.q: A distribution has a mean of 67 and a standard deviation of 4. Calculate its coefficient of variation in percent.
items.s: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (4/67) x 100 = 5.97 percent.

items.q: A box contains 9 red and 4 black balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.s: The box holds 13 balls in all, so P(red) = 9/13 = 0.6923.

items.q: A bag holds 20 balls of which 3 are red and 5 are blue. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red or blue?
items.s: Red and blue are mutually exclusive, so P = 3/20 + 5/20 = 0.4.

items.q: In how many ways can 9 distinct objects be arranged taken 3 at a time?
items.s: The number of arrangements is 9P3 = 9!/(9 - 3)! = 504.

items.q: In how many ways can a committee of 5 be chosen from 10 people?
items.s: The number of committees is 10C5 = 10!/(5!(10 - 5)!) = 252.

items.q: From 9 students a team of 3 is to be selected for a quiz and then 4 of the remaining students for a debate. In how many ways can both selections be made?
items.s: Choose the quiz team in 9C3 = 84 ways, then the debaters in 6C4 = 15 ways, so the total is 84 x 15 = 1260.

items.q: A binomial variable has 12 trials with probability of success 0.3 in each trial. Calculate its mean.
A binomial variable has 8 trials with probability of success 0.25 in each trial. Calculate its variance.
A normally distributed variable has mean 50 and standard deviation 12. Calculate the standard score of the value 26.
items.s: z = (x - mean)/standard deviation = (26 - 50)/12 = -2.

items.q: For 6 pairs of observations the sums of squares and products about the means are: sum of xy about the means = 50, sum of x squared about the mean = 40 and sum of y squared about the mean = 98. Calculate the coefficient of correlation.
items.s: r = sum(xy)/sqrt(sum(x squared) x sum(y squared)) = 50/sqrt(40 x 98) = 0.7986.

items.q: The regression line of y on x is y = 6 + 3x. Estimate the value of y when x = 4.
items.s: Substituting x = 4 gives y = 6 + 3 x 4 = 18.

items.q: A sample of 36 observations is drawn from a population with standard deviation 6. Calculate the standard error of the sample mean.
items.s: Standard error = standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 6/sqrt(36) = 1.

items.q: A sample of 25 has a known population standard deviation of 15. Taking the standard normal value as 1.96 for the required confidence level, calculate the half width of the confidence interval for the mean.
items.s: Half width = z x standard deviation/sqrt(n) = 1.96 x 15/sqrt(25) = 5.88.

items.q: A survey must estimate a mean to within 4 units with standard normal value 2, the population standard deviation being 20. Calculate the smallest sample size needed.
items.s: n = (z x standard deviation / margin)^2 = (2 x 20/4)^2 = 100, so the sample must be at least 100.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines classical probability?
o: the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
items.s: classical probability: the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes. The other options describe equally likely outcomes, random experiment, event.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts”
o: arithmetic mean
mode
decile
percentile
items.s: decile is one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines factorial?
o: the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order
a selection of objects in which the order of the objects does not matter
an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order
the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number
items.s: factorial: the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number. The other options describe binomial coefficient, arrangement with repetition, combination.

items.q: complementary event is best described as
o: the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question
a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all
items.s: complementary event: the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question. The other options describe conditional probability, impossible event, event.

items.q: Which of the following best describes probability distribution?
o: the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
a table, formula or graph that gives the chance of each value of a random variable
items.s: probability distribution: a table, formula or graph that gives the chance of each value of a random variable. The other options describe Bernoulli trial, Poisson process, cumulative probability.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines standardisation.
o: a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one
the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
the statement that the average of a large number of independent observations is approximately normally distributed whatever the shape of the original data
items.s: standardisation: the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread. The other options describe central limit result, standard normal variable, normal table.

items.q: Which term is described by “the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three”?
o: empirical rule
relative dispersion
standard deviation
coefficient of variation
items.s: empirical rule is the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines weighted mean.
o: the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
a distribution with a long tail to the left, where the mean is smaller than the median and the mode
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
items.s: weighted mean: an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance. The other options describe negatively skewed distribution, midpoint, median.

items.q: negative association is best described as
o: a plot of paired observations that shows whether the two quantities move together
a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises
the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible
a measure of agreement between two orderings of the same set of items
items.s: negative association: a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises. The other options describe least squares, rank correlation, scatter diagram.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Binomial and Poisson distributions?
o: discrete random variable
probability distribution
multiplication rule
expected value
items.s: Every other option belongs to Binomial and Poisson distributions. “multiplication rule” belongs to Elementary probability, not Binomial and Poisson distributions.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines complementary event?
o: a degree of belief assigned to an event by a judge rather than derived from counting or repetition
the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question
the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
items.s: complementary event: the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question. The other options describe equally likely outcomes, sample space, subjective probability.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a distribution in which every listed value of the variable has the same chance”
o: binomial setting
discrete random variable
uniform discrete distribution
Poisson process
items.s: uniform discrete distribution is a distribution in which every listed value of the variable has the same chance.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines tail area.
o: the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one
the number of standard deviations by which a value lies above or below the mean
items.s: tail area: the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value. The other options describe standard score, standard normal variable, normal table.

items.q: Which of the following best describes arithmetic mean?
o: the total of all the observations divided by the number of observations
a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change
items.s: arithmetic mean: the total of all the observations divided by the number of observations. The other options describe geometric average, grouped average, open end class.

items.q: equally likely outcomes may be defined as
o: a degree of belief assigned to an event by a judge rather than derived from counting or repetition
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions
items.s: equally likely outcomes: outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment. The other options describe relative frequency probability, subjective probability, random experiment.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Measures of dispersion?
o: range
interquartile range
quartile deviation
counting principle
items.s: Every other option belongs to Measures of dispersion. “counting principle” belongs to Permutations and combinations, not Measures of dispersion.

items.q: Which term is described by “two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening”?
o: sample space
impossible event
independent events
exhaustive events
items.s: independent events is two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening.

items.q: expected value may be defined as
o: a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
the use of a count distribution with mean equal to the product of trials and chance when the number of trials is large and the chance of success is small
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value
items.s: expected value: the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value. The other options describe Poisson approximation, Bernoulli trial, binomial setting.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines quartile deviation.
o: the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile
the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
items.s: quartile deviation: half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile. The other options describe population variance, degrees of freedom, standard deviation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines sampling distribution?
o: the pattern of values a statistic would take if the same sized samples were drawn again and again
the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size
a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average
an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population
items.s: sampling distribution: the pattern of values a statistic would take if the same sized samples were drawn again and again. The other options describe standard error, parameter, non sampling error.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Measures of central tendency?
o: arithmetic mean
parameter
median
mode
items.s: Every other option belongs to Measures of central tendency. “parameter” belongs to Sampling and estimation, not Measures of central tendency.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines negative association?
o: the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it
a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises
the square of the correlation coefficient, giving the proportion of the variation in one quantity explained by the other
a number between minus one and plus one that measures the strength and direction of a straight line relationship
items.s: negative association: a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises. The other options describe product moment coefficient, coefficient of determination, extrapolation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines population variance?
o: the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations
the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile
the difference between the upper and the lower quartile of an ordered set of data
items.s: population variance: the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean. The other options describe sample variance, quartile deviation, interquartile range.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines discrete random variable.
o: the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance
a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
items.s: discrete random variable: a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance. The other options describe binomial setting, cumulative probability, Bernoulli trial.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question”
o: relative frequency probability
complementary event
equally likely outcomes
multiplication rule
items.s: complementary event is the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question.

items.q: Which of the following best describes midpoint?
o: the total of all the observations divided by the number of observations
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
a distribution with a long tail to the left, where the mean is smaller than the median and the mode
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
items.s: midpoint: the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval. The other options describe arithmetic mean, weighted mean, negatively skewed distribution.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three”
o: relative dispersion
quartile deviation
sample variance
empirical rule
items.s: empirical rule is the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines mean squared deviation?
o: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
the average of the absolute differences between each observation and a chosen average
half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets
items.s: mean squared deviation: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them. The other options describe mean deviation, coefficient of variation, quartile deviation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the half width of the interval placed about an estimate”?
o: unbiased estimator
systematic selection
sampling error
margin of error
items.s: margin of error is the half width of the interval placed about an estimate.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines percentile?
o: a distribution with a long tail to the left, where the mean is smaller than the median and the mode
a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
the number of observations divided by the sum of their reciprocals, used for average speeds
items.s: percentile: one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts. The other options describe negatively skewed distribution, harmonic average, open end class.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value”
o: unbiased estimator
standard error
quota selection
parameter
items.s: unbiased estimator is a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value.

items.q: Three of these relate to Elementary probability. Which one does not?
o: simple random selection
sample space
random experiment
event
items.s: Every other option belongs to Elementary probability. “simple random selection” belongs to Sampling and estimation, not Elementary probability.

items.q: Which of the following best describes expected value?
o: a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value
a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
items.s: expected value: the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value. The other options describe binomial setting, Bernoulli trial, Poisson process.

items.q: Which of the following best describes negatively skewed distribution?
o: the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
a distribution with a long tail to the left, where the mean is smaller than the median and the mode
one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
items.s: negatively skewed distribution: a distribution with a long tail to the left, where the mean is smaller than the median and the mode. The other options describe median, percentile, midpoint.

items.q: Three of these relate to Measures of dispersion. Which one does not?
o: interquartile range
range
quartile deviation
addition rule
items.s: Every other option belongs to Measures of dispersion. “addition rule” belongs to Elementary probability, not Measures of dispersion.

items.q: standard deviation may be defined as
o: a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile
the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean
the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations
items.s: standard deviation: the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean. The other options describe quartile deviation, sample variance, relative dispersion.

items.q: Which of the following best describes combined average?
o: the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data
an observation that lies far away from the rest of the data and pulls an average towards it
a class interval that has only one stated limit, so its midpoint cannot be fixed without an assumption
the single average obtained for two or more groups after pooling their totals and their counts
items.s: combined average: the single average obtained for two or more groups after pooling their totals and their counts. The other options describe outlier, open end class, mode.

items.q: combination may be defined as
o: a selection of objects in which the order of the objects does not matter
an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order
the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number
an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters
items.s: combination: a selection of objects in which the order of the objects does not matter. The other options describe arrangement with repetition, factorial, permutation.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both”
o: mutually exclusive events
addition rule
complementary event
independent events
items.s: addition rule is the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both.

items.q: Which of the following best describes coefficient of determination?
o: a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
a strong link between two quantities that arises only because both are driven by a third quantity
a number between minus one and plus one that measures the strength and direction of a straight line relationship
the square of the correlation coefficient, giving the proportion of the variation in one quantity explained by the other
items.s: coefficient of determination: the square of the correlation coefficient, giving the proportion of the variation in one quantity explained by the other. The other options describe positive association, product moment coefficient, spurious association.

items.q: Which of the following best describes counting principle?
o: the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number
an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once
an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters
the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways
items.s: counting principle: the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways. The other options describe permutation, circular arrangement, factorial.

items.q: sample variance is best described as
o: a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations
items.s: sample variance: the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations. The other options describe degrees of freedom, relative dispersion, coefficient of variation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines geometric average?
o: a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode
one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts
the total of all the observations divided by the number of observations
the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change
items.s: geometric average: the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change. The other options describe positively skewed distribution, decile, arithmetic mean.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines quartile deviation?
o: the average of the absolute differences between each observation and a chosen average
the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile
the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations
items.s: quartile deviation: half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile. The other options describe population variance, sample variance, mean deviation.

items.q: independent events may be defined as
o: two or more events that cannot happen at the same time
two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening
a degree of belief assigned to an event by a judge rather than derived from counting or repetition
an event that contains no outcome of the sample space at all
items.s: independent events: two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening. The other options describe mutually exclusive events, subjective probability, impossible event.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate”
o: sampling distribution
confidence interval
sampling error
unbiased estimator
items.s: confidence interval is a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate.

items.q: classical probability may be defined as
o: two or more events that cannot happen at the same time
the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question
items.s: classical probability: the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes. The other options describe complementary event, conditional probability, mutually exclusive events.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes”
o: cumulative probability
expected value
Poisson process
binomial setting
items.s: binomial setting is a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread”
o: inflection point
standardisation
normal table
standard normal variable
items.s: standardisation is the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines uniform discrete distribution.
o: the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
a distribution in which every listed value of the variable has the same chance
a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance
a table, formula or graph that gives the chance of each value of a random variable
items.s: uniform discrete distribution: a distribution in which every listed value of the variable has the same chance. The other options describe discrete random variable, cumulative probability, probability distribution.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines coefficient of determination.
o: a plot of paired observations that shows whether the two quantities move together
the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it
a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
the square of the correlation coefficient, giving the proportion of the variation in one quantity explained by the other
items.s: coefficient of determination: the square of the correlation coefficient, giving the proportion of the variation in one quantity explained by the other. The other options describe scatter diagram, extrapolation, positive association.

items.q: sampling error is best described as
o: the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used
a method in which a starting point is chosen at random and every kth member of the list is then taken
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value
items.s: sampling error: the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used. The other options describe systematic selection, point estimate, cluster selection.

items.q: exhaustive events may be defined as
o: a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening
the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question
a degree of belief assigned to an event by a judge rather than derived from counting or repetition
items.s: exhaustive events: a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment. The other options describe subjective probability, independent events, complementary event.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines standard error.
o: a complete list of the members of a population from which a selection is made
the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size
a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value
a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average
items.s: standard error: the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size. The other options describe sampling frame, statistic, parameter.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines statistic.
o: the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used
a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
items.s: statistic: a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value. The other options describe cluster selection, sampling error, margin of error.

items.q: Which term is described by “the number of observations divided by the sum of their reciprocals, used for average speeds”?
o: harmonic average
quartile
weighted mean
percentile
items.s: harmonic average is the number of observations divided by the sum of their reciprocals, used for average speeds.

items.q: systematic selection is best described as
o: the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
a method in which a starting point is chosen at random and every kth member of the list is then taken
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
items.s: systematic selection: a method in which a starting point is chosen at random and every kth member of the list is then taken. The other options describe population, margin of error, cluster selection.

items.q: binomial setting is best described as
o: a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
a distribution in which every listed value of the variable has the same chance
the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
items.s: binomial setting: a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes. The other options describe uniform discrete distribution, Poisson process, cumulative probability.

items.q: random experiment may be defined as
o: the relation that the chance of two events happening together is the chance of the first times the conditional chance of the second
a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions
items.s: random experiment: a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out. The other options describe exhaustive events, multiplication rule, relative frequency probability.

items.q: Which term is described by “a plot of paired observations that shows whether the two quantities move together”?
o: spurious association
scatter diagram
regression coefficient
zero association
items.s: scatter diagram is a plot of paired observations that shows whether the two quantities move together.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it”
o: extrapolation
product moment coefficient
negative association
coefficient of determination
items.s: extrapolation is the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines population?
o: an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population
a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size
the difference between a sample result and the true population value that arises because only part of the population is used
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
items.s: population: the whole set of items about which information is wanted. The other options describe stratified selection, sampling error, non sampling error.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines permutation?
o: the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number
an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters
the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways
an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order
items.s: permutation: an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters. The other options describe arrangement with repetition, counting principle, factorial.

items.q: Which of the following best describes coefficient of variation?
o: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets
items.s: coefficient of variation: the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets. The other options describe relative dispersion, mean squared deviation, population variance.

items.q: Which of the following best describes weighted mean?
o: the single average obtained for two or more groups after pooling their totals and their counts
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
the observation that occurs most frequently in a set of data
one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts
items.s: weighted mean: an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance. The other options describe combined average, mode, decile.

items.q: For 6 pairs of observations the sums of squares and products about the means are: sum of xy about the means = 65, sum of x squared about the mean = 79 and sum of y squared about the mean = 84. Calculate the coefficient of correlation.
items.s: r = sum(xy)/sqrt(sum(x squared) x sum(y squared)) = 65/sqrt(79 x 84) = 0.7979.

items.q: A survey must estimate a mean to within 2 units with standard normal value 1.96, the population standard deviation being 10. Calculate the smallest sample size needed.
items.s: n = (z x standard deviation / margin)^2 = (1.96 x 10/2)^2 = 96.04, so the sample must be at least 97.

items.q: The scores obtained by five students in a test are 5, 32, 39, 51, 57. Calculate the mean score.
items.s: Mean = sum of scores / number of scores = 184 / 5 = 36.8.

items.q: The values 9, 27, 42, 56, 59 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: Arranged in order the third value is the median, so the median is 42.

items.q: The values 8, 10, 52, 54, 60, 79 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: With six values the median is the mean of the third and fourth: (52 + 54)/2 = 53.

items.q: The values 30, 30, 37, 49, 31, 30 were recorded. State the mode.
items.s: The value 30 occurs three times, more often than any other, so the mode is 30.

items.q: A grouped frequency table has midpoint 15 with frequency 3; midpoint 65 with frequency 5; midpoint 85 with frequency 9. Calculate the mean of the distribution.
items.s: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 1135 and total frequency = 17, so the mean is 1135/17 = 66.76.

items.q: A class of 14 students has a mean score of 40 while another class of 9 students has a mean score of 72. Calculate the mean score of the two classes combined.
The values 13, 26, 34, 40, 45 were recorded. Calculate the range.
items.s: Range = largest - smallest = 45 - 13 = 32.

items.q: The values 10, 16, 24, 31, 37 form a complete population. Calculate the population variance.
items.s: The mean is 23.6. Sum of squared deviations is 477.2, so the variance is that sum divided by 5 = 95.44.

items.q: The values 9, 18, 26, 32, 37, 38 are a sample drawn from a large population. Calculate the sample variance.
items.s: The mean is 26.67 and the sum of squared deviations is 651.3. Dividing by n - 1 = 5 gives 130.3.

items.q: The values 6, 13, 25, 32, 42 are a sample. Calculate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 23.6, the sum of squared deviations is 833.2, and the variance is 208.3. Its square root gives a standard deviation of 14.43.

items.q: A distribution has a mean of 74 and a standard deviation of 4. Calculate its coefficient of variation in percent.
items.s: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (4/74) x 100 = 5.41 percent.

items.q: The values 9, 24, 39, 44, 55, 63, 65 are arranged in order. Taking the second and sixth values as the lower and upper quartiles, calculate the quartile deviation.
items.s: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2 = (63 - 24)/2 = 19.5.

items.q: A box contains 3 red and 5 black balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.s: The box holds 8 balls in all, so P(red) = 3/8 = 0.375.

items.q: A bag holds 20 balls of which 7 are red and 6 are blue. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red or blue?
items.s: Red and blue are mutually exclusive, so P = 7/20 + 6/20 = 0.65.

items.q: In a class, the probability that a student offers Physics is 3/10 and the probability that a student offers Chemistry is 5/10. The probability of offering both is 2/10. What is the probability that a student offers Physics or Chemistry?
In how many ways can a committee of 4 be chosen from 6 people?
items.s: The number of committees is 6C4 = 6!/(4!(6 - 4)!) = 15.

items.q: A fair experiment is repeated 6 times and the probability of success in a single trial is 0.3. Calculate the probability of exactly 0 successes.
A binomial variable has 16 trials with probability of success 0.5 in each trial. Calculate its mean.
items.s: Mean = np = 16 x 0.5 = 8.

items.q: A binomial variable has 18 trials with probability of success 0.2 in each trial. Calculate its variance.
A normally distributed variable has mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Calculate the standard score of the value 115.
items.s: z = (x - mean)/standard deviation = (115 - 100)/15 = 1.

items.q: A normal variable has mean 40 and standard deviation 4. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413 and between the mean and two standard deviations is 0.4772, find the probability that a value is less than 48.
items.s: The value 48 is 2 standard deviation(s) above the mean, so the probability is 0.5 + 0.4772 = 0.9772.

items.q: For a set of paired observations the sum of xy about the means is 75 and the sum of x squared about the mean is 22. Calculate the slope of the regression line of y on x.
items.s: Slope b = sum(xy)/sum(x squared) = 75/22 = 3.41.

items.q: The regression line of y on x is y = 8 + 1.5x. Estimate the value of y when x = 7.
items.s: Substituting x = 7 gives y = 8 + 1.5 x 7 = 18.5.

items.q: A sample of 16 observations is drawn from a population with standard deviation 12. Calculate the standard error of the sample mean.
items.s: Standard error = standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 12/sqrt(16) = 3.

items.q: From 11 students a team of 3 is to be selected for a quiz and then 4 of the remaining students for a debate. In how many ways can both selections be made?
items.s: Choose the quiz team in 11C3 = 165 ways, then the debaters in 8C4 = 70 ways, so the total is 165 x 70 = 11550.

items.q: The number of calls arriving at a switchboard follows a Poisson distribution with mean 2 per minute. Calculate the probability of exactly 2 calls in a minute.

For 5 pairs of observations the sums of squares and products about the means are: sum of xy about the means = 47, sum of x squared about the mean = 57 and sum of y squared about the mean = 61. Calculate the coefficient of correlation.
items.s: r = sum(xy)/sqrt(sum(x squared) x sum(y squared)) = 47/sqrt(57 x 61) = 0.7971.

items.q: A sample of 36 has a known population standard deviation of 10. Taking the standard normal value as 2.58 for the required confidence level, calculate the half width of the confidence interval for the mean.
items.s: Half width = z x standard deviation/sqrt(n) = 2.58 x 10/sqrt(36) = 4.3.

items.q: A survey must estimate a mean to within 4 units with standard normal value 2, the population standard deviation being 10. Calculate the smallest sample size needed.
items.s: n = (z x standard deviation / margin)^2 = (2 x 10/4)^2 = 25, so the sample must be at least 25.

items.q: The scores obtained by five students in a test are 21, 25, 33, 53, 57. Calculate the mean score.
items.s: Mean = sum of scores / number of scores = 189 / 5 = 37.8.

items.q: The values 14, 18, 38, 43, 56 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: Arranged in order the third value is the median, so the median is 38.

items.q: The values 18, 33, 42, 43, 68, 75 were observed in a sample. Calculate the median.
items.s: With six values the median is the mean of the third and fourth: (42 + 43)/2 = 42.5.

items.q: The values 49, 5, 5, 67, 41, 5 were recorded. State the mode.
items.s: The value 5 occurs three times, more often than any other, so the mode is 5.

items.q: A grouped frequency table has midpoint 35 with frequency 8; midpoint 45 with frequency 3; midpoint 85 with frequency 7. Calculate the mean of the distribution.
items.s: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 1010 and total frequency = 18, so the mean is 1010/18 = 56.11.

items.q: A class of 19 students has a mean score of 40 while another class of 16 students has a mean score of 63. Calculate the mean score of the two classes combined.
The values 4, 18, 42, 82, 83 were recorded. Calculate the range.
items.s: Range = largest - smallest = 83 - 4 = 79.

items.q: The values 3, 5, 8, 30, 39 form a complete population. Calculate the population variance.
items.s: The mean is 17. Sum of squared deviations is 1074, so the variance is that sum divided by 5 = 214.8.

items.q: The values 4, 14, 16, 25, 30, 33 are a sample drawn from a large population. Calculate the sample variance.
items.s: The mean is 20.33 and the sum of squared deviations is 601.3. Dividing by n - 1 = 5 gives 120.3.

items.q: The values 21, 30, 32, 34, 35 are a sample. Calculate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: The mean is 30.4, the sum of squared deviations is 125.2, and the variance is 31.3. Its square root gives a standard deviation of 5.59.

items.q: A distribution has a mean of 44 and a standard deviation of 4. Calculate its coefficient of variation in percent.
items.s: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (4/44) x 100 = 9.09 percent.

items.q: The values 5, 8, 15, 28, 36, 50, 78 are arranged in order. Taking the second and sixth values as the lower and upper quartiles, calculate the quartile deviation.
items.s: Quartile deviation = (Q3 - Q1)/2 = (50 - 8)/2 = 21.

items.q: A box contains 9 red and 5 black balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.s: The box holds 14 balls in all, so P(red) = 9/14 = 0.6429.

items.q: A bag holds 20 balls of which 2 are red and 2 are blue. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red or blue?
items.s: Red and blue are mutually exclusive, so P = 2/20 + 2/20 = 0.2.

items.q: In a class, the probability that a student offers Physics is 4/10 and the probability that a student offers Chemistry is 6/10. The probability of offering both is 1/10. What is the probability that a student offers Physics or Chemistry?
The probability that an event happens is 0.15. Calculate the probability that it does not happen.
In how many ways can 8 distinct objects be arranged taken 2 at a time?
items.s: The number of arrangements is 8P2 = 8!/(8 - 2)! = 56.

items.q: In how many ways can a committee of 2 be chosen from 9 people?
items.s: The number of committees is 9C2 = 9!/(2!(9 - 2)!) = 36.

items.q: A fair experiment is repeated 4 times and the probability of success in a single trial is 0.2. Calculate the probability of exactly 0 successes.
A binomial variable has 8 trials with probability of success 0.25 in each trial. Calculate its mean.
items.s: Mean = np = 8 x 0.25 = 2.

items.q: A binomial variable has 16 trials with probability of success 0.4 in each trial. Calculate its variance.
A normally distributed variable has mean 50 and standard deviation 15. Calculate the standard score of the value 20.
items.s: z = (x - mean)/standard deviation = (20 - 50)/15 = -2.

items.q: A normal variable has mean 60 and standard deviation 5. Using the table value that the area between the mean and one standard deviation is 0.3413 and between the mean and two standard deviations is 0.4772, find the probability that a value is less than 65.
items.s: The value 65 is 1 standard deviation(s) above the mean, so the probability is 0.5 + 0.3413 = 0.8413.

items.q: For a set of paired observations the sum of xy about the means is 126 and the sum of x squared about the mean is 29. Calculate the slope of the regression line of y on x.
items.s: Slope b = sum(xy)/sum(x squared) = 126/29 = 4.34.

items.q: The regression line of y on x is y = 5 + 2x. Estimate the value of y when x = 12.
items.s: Substituting x = 12 gives y = 5 + 2 x 12 = 29.

items.q: A sample of 25 observations is drawn from a population with standard deviation 6. Calculate the standard error of the sample mean.
items.s: Standard error = standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 6/sqrt(25) = 1.2.

items.q: From 11 students a team of 2 is to be selected for a quiz and then 4 of the remaining students for a debate. In how many ways can both selections be made?
items.s: Choose the quiz team in 11C2 = 55 ways, then the debaters in 9C4 = 126 ways, so the total is 55 x 126 = 6930.

items.q: For 5 pairs of observations the sums of squares and products about the means are: sum of xy about the means = 39, sum of x squared about the mean = 49 and sum of y squared about the mean = 51. Calculate the coefficient of correlation.
items.s: r = sum(xy)/sqrt(sum(x squared) x sum(y squared)) = 39/sqrt(49 x 51) = 0.7802.

items.q: A survey must estimate a mean to within 5 units with standard normal value 1.96, the population standard deviation being 10. Calculate the smallest sample size needed.
items.s: n = (z x standard deviation / margin)^2 = (1.96 x 10/5)^2 = 15.37, so the sample must be at least 16.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains random experiment.
o: the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
items.s: random experiment: a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out. The other options describe classical probability, independent events, equally likely outcomes.

items.q: The correct meaning of circular arrangement is
o: an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once
an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters
the number of ways of choosing a stated number of objects from a larger group without regard to order
the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number
items.s: circular arrangement: an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once. The other options describe permutation, factorial, binomial coefficient.

items.q: “a method in which every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen and every group of the required size has an equal chance” is the definition of
o: standard error
simple random selection
sampling frame
cluster selection
items.s: simple random selection is a method in which every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen and every group of the required size has an equal chance.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains mean squared deviation.
o: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them
a measure of dispersion that keeps the original units of the data
the average of the absolute differences between each observation and a chosen average
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
items.s: mean squared deviation: the quantity obtained by squaring each deviation from the mean before averaging them. The other options describe absolute measure of spread, degrees of freedom, mean deviation.

items.q: The correct meaning of addition rule is
o: the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both
the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
items.s: addition rule: the relation that the chance of either of two events is the sum of their separate chances less the chance of both. The other options describe exhaustive events, conditional probability, equally likely outcomes.

items.q: The correct meaning of margin of error is
o: a method in which every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen and every group of the required size has an equal chance
a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average
a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value
the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
items.s: margin of error: the half width of the interval placed about an estimate. The other options describe simple random selection, point estimate, parameter.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “two or more events that cannot happen at the same time”
o: independent events
event
complementary event
mutually exclusive events
items.s: mutually exclusive events is two or more events that cannot happen at the same time.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines binomial setting?
o: the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value
a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
a table, formula or graph that gives the chance of each value of a random variable
items.s: binomial setting: a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes. The other options describe expected value, probability distribution, cumulative probability.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains arrangement with repetition.
o: the product of all the whole numbers from one up to a given number
an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order
an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters
the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways
items.s: arrangement with repetition: an ordering in which some of the objects are identical, so swapping them does not create a new order. The other options describe counting principle, permutation, factorial.

items.q: “the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value” is the definition of
o: standardisation
normal curve
tail area
normal approximation
items.s: tail area is the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value.

items.q: “a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes” is the definition of
o: Bernoulli trial
cumulative probability
binomial setting
discrete random variable
items.s: binomial setting is a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes.

items.q: “a method in which interviewers fill fixed numbers of respondents in stated categories, without random drawing” is the definition of
o: unbiased estimator
standard error
sampling error
quota selection
items.s: quota selection is a method in which interviewers fill fixed numbers of respondents in stated categories, without random drawing.

items.q: In this course, point estimate refers to
o: a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value
a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value
a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate
items.s: point estimate: a single number calculated from a sample and used as the best guess of a population value. The other options describe confidence interval, statistic, cluster selection.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains positively skewed distribution.
o: the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change
a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode
one of the nine values that divide an ordered set of data into ten equal parts
items.s: positively skewed distribution: a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode. The other options describe decile, geometric average, median.

items.q: The correct meaning of classical probability is
o: two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening
the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
the relation that the chance of two events happening together is the chance of the first times the conditional chance of the second
the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
items.s: classical probability: the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes. The other options describe conditional probability, independent events, multiplication rule.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines symmetrical distribution?
o: an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide
the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
items.s: symmetrical distribution: a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide. The other options describe grouped average, weighted mean, percentile.
