items.q: Which statement correctly defines expected value?
o: a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance
a table, formula or graph that gives the chance of each value of a random variable
a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value
items.s: expected value: the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value. The other options describe Poisson process, discrete random variable, probability distribution.

items.q: In this course, stratified selection refers to
o: a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size
a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate
a method in which whole groups such as classes or villages are chosen at random and every member of a chosen group is used
the half width of the interval placed about an estimate
items.s: stratified selection: a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size. The other options describe cluster selection, confidence interval, margin of error.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one”
o: normal approximation
standard normal variable
normal table
normal curve
items.s: standard normal variable is a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines range?
o: the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
a measure of dispersion that keeps the original units of the data
items.s: range: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data. The other options describe absolute measure of spread, empirical rule, degrees of freedom.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains range.
o: the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
the difference between the upper and the lower quartile of an ordered set of data
items.s: range: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data. The other options describe population variance, empirical rule, interquartile range.

items.q: In this course, range refers to
o: half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile
the average of the squared deviations of all the observations from their mean
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
items.s: range: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data. The other options describe degrees of freedom, population variance, quartile deviation.

items.q: “the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways” is the definition of
o: combination
counting principle
factorial
circular arrangement
items.s: counting principle is the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains sample space.
o: a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment
the relation that the chance of two events happening together is the chance of the first times the conditional chance of the second
outcomes that have the same chance of occurring in a given experiment
items.s: sample space: the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment. The other options describe equally likely outcomes, event, multiplication rule.

items.q: In this course, degrees of freedom refers to
o: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations
the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data
the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean
items.s: degrees of freedom: the number of independent pieces of information left after one or more quantities have been estimated from the data. The other options describe standard deviation, sample variance, range.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines relative dispersion?
o: the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets
a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation in a set of data
half of the difference between the upper and the lower quartile
items.s: relative dispersion: a measure of spread stated as a ratio or percentage so that data sets with different units can be compared. The other options describe coefficient of variation, quartile deviation, range.

items.q: relative frequency probability may be defined as
o: the relation that the chance of two events happening together is the chance of the first times the conditional chance of the second
the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions
the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
items.s: relative frequency probability: the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions. The other options describe event, conditional probability, multiplication rule.

items.q: The correct meaning of normal approximation is
o: the number of standard deviations by which a value lies above or below the mean
the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
items.s: normal approximation: the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large. The other options describe tail area, standard score, normal table.

items.q: The correct meaning of binomial setting is
o: the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
items.s: binomial setting: a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes. The other options describe Bernoulli trial, Poisson process, cumulative probability.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines grouped average?
o: the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies
the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
items.s: grouped average: the average of a frequency table computed from class midpoints and their frequencies. The other options describe midpoint, percentile, median.

items.q: “the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three” is the definition of
o: mean squared deviation
empirical rule
coefficient of variation
quartile deviation
items.s: empirical rule is the statement that for mound shaped data about 68 per cent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95 per cent within two and about 99.7 per cent within three.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains symmetrical distribution.
o: one of the three values that divide an ordered set of data into four equal parts
the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide
items.s: symmetrical distribution: a distribution in which the two halves about the centre are mirror images, so the three averages coincide. The other options describe weighted mean, quartile, median.

items.q: scatter diagram may be defined as
o: a plot of paired observations that shows whether the two quantities move together
a strong link between two quantities that arises only because both are driven by a third quantity
a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
the straight line that gives the best estimate of one quantity from a stated value of the other
items.s: scatter diagram: a plot of paired observations that shows whether the two quantities move together. The other options describe regression line, positive association, spurious association.

items.q: In this course, positive association refers to
o: a measure of agreement between two orderings of the same set of items
a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible
a strong link between two quantities that arises only because both are driven by a third quantity
items.s: positive association: a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises. The other options describe rank correlation, spurious association, least squares.

items.q: In this course, Poisson approximation refers to
o: the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value
the use of a count distribution with mean equal to the product of trials and chance when the number of trials is large and the chance of success is small
items.s: Poisson approximation: the use of a count distribution with mean equal to the product of trials and chance when the number of trials is large and the chance of success is small. The other options describe binomial setting, cumulative probability, expected value.

items.q: “the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment” is the definition of
o: subjective probability
multiplication rule
sample space
relative frequency probability
items.s: sample space is the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment.

items.q: “the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it” is the definition of
o: extrapolation
spurious association
regression line
product moment coefficient
items.s: extrapolation is the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains parameter.
o: a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average
an inaccuracy that comes from faults in measurement, recording, coverage or response rather than from using only part of the population
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
the pattern of values a statistic would take if the same sized samples were drawn again and again
items.s: parameter: a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average. The other options describe sampling distribution, non sampling error, population.

items.q: Three of these relate to Permutations and combinations. Which one does not?
o: combination
mode
factorial
permutation
items.s: Every other option belongs to Permutations and combinations. “mode” belongs to Measures of central tendency, not Permutations and combinations.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains midpoint.
o: the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
an observation that lies far away from the rest of the data and pulls an average towards it
the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
items.s: midpoint: the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval. The other options describe outlier, weighted mean, median.

items.q: Poisson process may be defined as
o: the chance that a random variable takes a value no greater than a stated value
a table, formula or graph that gives the chance of each value of a random variable
a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
items.s: Poisson process: a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate. The other options describe binomial setting, probability distribution, cumulative probability.

items.q: “the statement that the average of a large number of independent observations is approximately normally distributed whatever the shape of the original data” is the definition of
o: normal curve
standard normal variable
standardisation
central limit result
items.s: central limit result is the statement that the average of a large number of independent observations is approximately normally distributed whatever the shape of the original data.

items.q: The correct meaning of normal curve is
o: the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
a continuous bell shaped curve that is symmetric about its centre and fixed by its mean and its spread
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
items.s: normal curve: a continuous bell shaped curve that is symmetric about its centre and fixed by its mean and its spread. The other options describe normal table, standardisation, tail area.

items.q: The correct meaning of parameter is
o: a range of values, built from sample data, that is expected to contain the population value with a stated long run success rate
a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average
a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size
a rule for estimating a population value whose average over repeated samples equals the true value
items.s: parameter: a numerical characteristic of a whole population, such as its average. The other options describe confidence interval, unbiased estimator, stratified selection.

items.q: The correct meaning of weighted mean is
o: the number of observations divided by the sum of their reciprocals, used for average speeds
a distribution with a long tail to the left, where the mean is smaller than the median and the mode
a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
items.s: weighted mean: an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance. The other options describe positively skewed distribution, negatively skewed distribution, harmonic average.

items.q: The correct meaning of rank correlation is
o: a number between minus one and plus one that measures the strength and direction of a straight line relationship
a strong link between two quantities that arises only because both are driven by a third quantity
the rule that fixes the estimating line by making the sum of the squared vertical deviations as small as possible
a measure of agreement between two orderings of the same set of items
items.s: rank correlation: a measure of agreement between two orderings of the same set of items. The other options describe least squares, spurious association, product moment coefficient.

items.q: In this course, expected value refers to
o: a variable that can take only separate countable values, each with a stated chance
a count of events in a fixed interval where the events occur independently at a constant average rate
a distribution in which every listed value of the variable has the same chance
the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value
items.s: expected value: the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value. The other options describe uniform discrete distribution, Poisson process, discrete random variable.

items.q: coefficient of determination may be defined as
o: the use of an estimating line to predict far outside the range of the data that produced it
a relationship in which no tendency for the two quantities to move together can be seen
the square of the correlation coefficient, giving the proportion of the variation in one quantity explained by the other
a measure of agreement between two orderings of the same set of items
items.s: coefficient of determination: the square of the correlation coefficient, giving the proportion of the variation in one quantity explained by the other. The other options describe zero association, rank correlation, extrapolation.

items.q: “the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets” is the definition of
o: empirical rule
coefficient of variation
interquartile range
mean squared deviation
items.s: coefficient of variation is the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare spread between data sets.

items.q: circular arrangement may be defined as
o: an arrangement of objects in which the order of the objects matters
the rule that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways then the two together can be done in m times n ways
an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once
a selection of objects in which the order of the objects does not matter
items.s: circular arrangement: an ordering of objects around a ring, where rotations of the same ordering are counted once. The other options describe counting principle, combination, permutation.

items.q: In this course, median refers to
o: a distribution with a long tail to the right, where the mean exceeds the median and the median exceeds the mode
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size
one of the ninety nine values that divide an ordered set of data into a hundred equal parts
items.s: median: the middle value of a set of observations arranged in order of size. The other options describe percentile, weighted mean, positively skewed distribution.

items.q: The correct meaning of complementary event is
o: a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
two or more events whose occurrence does not alter the chance of the others happening
the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions
the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question
items.s: complementary event: the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question. The other options describe relative frequency probability, independent events, exhaustive events.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines positive association?
o: a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises
a relationship in which no tendency for the two quantities to move together can be seen
a relationship in which one quantity tends to fall as the other rises
a strong link between two quantities that arises only because both are driven by a third quantity
items.s: positive association: a relationship in which one quantity tends to rise as the other rises. The other options describe spurious association, zero association, negative association.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains normal approximation.
o: the operation of subtracting the mean from a value and dividing the result by the spread
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
the point on the bell curve where it changes from bending downwards to bending upwards, found one standard deviation from the centre
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
items.s: normal approximation: the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large. The other options describe inflection point, standardisation, normal table.

items.q: The correct meaning of normal table is
o: the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
the point on the bell curve where it changes from bending downwards to bending upwards, found one standard deviation from the centre
items.s: normal table: a published set of areas under the standard bell curve used to obtain chances without integration. The other options describe tail area, inflection point, normal approximation.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains conditional probability.
o: a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
the proportion of times an event has occurred in a long series of repetitions
the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened
the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
items.s: conditional probability: the chance of one event given that another event is known to have happened. The other options describe classical probability, relative frequency probability, event.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines weighted mean?
o: an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
one of the three values that divide an ordered set of data into four equal parts
the total of all the observations divided by the number of observations
the value halfway between the lower and upper limits of a class interval
items.s: weighted mean: an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance. The other options describe midpoint, quartile, arithmetic mean.

items.q: The correct meaning of standard score is
o: the number of standard deviations by which a value lies above or below the mean
the part of the area under a curve that lies beyond a stated value
the use of a bell curve to estimate chances for a count variable when the number of trials is large
a normally distributed quantity that has been rescaled to have a mean of zero and a spread of one
items.s: standard score: the number of standard deviations by which a value lies above or below the mean. The other options describe tail area, normal approximation, standard normal variable.

items.q: The correct meaning of uniform discrete distribution is
o: a fixed number of independent trials, each with the same chance of success and only two possible outcomes
the sum of each value of a random variable multiplied by the chance of that value
a single trial with exactly two possible outcomes, usually called success and failure
a distribution in which every listed value of the variable has the same chance
items.s: uniform discrete distribution: a distribution in which every listed value of the variable has the same chance. The other options describe expected value, Bernoulli trial, binomial setting.

items.q: The correct meaning of statistic is
o: a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value
a method in which a starting point is chosen at random and every kth member of the list is then taken
a method in which the population is first split into groups and members are then drawn from each group in proportion to its size
the spread of the values a statistic takes over repeated samples of the same size
items.s: statistic: a numerical characteristic computed from a sample, used to estimate a population value. The other options describe standard error, stratified selection, systematic selection.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines exhaustive events?
o: a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is carried out
the event that consists of every outcome in the sample space except those of the event in question
a collection of outcomes of a random experiment that is of interest
a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
items.s: exhaustive events: a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment. The other options describe event, random experiment, complementary event.

items.q: “a selection of objects in which the order of the objects does not matter” is the definition of
o: circular arrangement
combination
arrangement with repetition
counting principle
items.s: combination is a selection of objects in which the order of the objects does not matter.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains arithmetic mean.
o: one of the three values that divide an ordered set of data into four equal parts
the total of all the observations divided by the number of observations
the nth root of the product of n positive observations, used for rates of change
an average in which each observation is scaled by a factor that shows its relative importance
items.s: arithmetic mean: the total of all the observations divided by the number of observations. The other options describe weighted mean, geometric average, quartile.

items.q: In this course, exhaustive events refers to
o: two or more events that cannot happen at the same time
the ratio of the number of favourable outcomes to the number of equally likely outcomes
the relation that the chance of two events happening together is the chance of the first times the conditional chance of the second
a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment
items.s: exhaustive events: a set of events that together cover every possible outcome of the experiment. The other options describe classical probability, mutually exclusive events, multiplication rule.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean”
o: mean squared deviation
quartile deviation
degrees of freedom
standard deviation
items.s: standard deviation is the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations from the mean.
